# Ambiguous-Requirement Scenario (SCN-C) Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate the Scenario C design for detection, prevention, clarification, impact, and resume
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Legend**: `[M]` mandatory (a constitution MUST, an approved requirement, or an approved decision); `[O]` optional enhancement or backlog boundary. `G0` is evaluable now against the approved specification, plan, ADRs, and contracts; `G1` is evaluable after `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-analyze`, before implementation. `{Detects: ...}` links an item to a failure pattern in the [README](README.md) detection matrix. Dimension tags: Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Measurability, Coverage, Traceability, Edge Case, Assumption, Conflict, Gap.
## Detection and Classification

- [ ] CHK001 - Is each problematic statement in the Scenario C input listed with its classification rationale? [Completeness, Scenario C §3] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are detection rules (conflict, undefined term, testability) defined as deterministic, with the expected classification per statement? [Measurability, Spec FR-111, DEC-047] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is "material" defined by criteria (API contract, persistence schema, security boundary, orchestration flow) and "non-material" by a safe documented default? [Clarity, Spec DEC-047] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is the case of conflict with approved requirements routed through change approval rather than silently accepted? [Coverage, Spec FR-126] [M, G0]

## Prevention, Clarification, Resume

- [ ] CHK005 - Is prevention of unsafe implementation defined as an observable refusal (entry criteria unmet, denied, audited)? [Coverage, Spec FR-113 NAC, FR-104] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is silent resolution of a material ambiguity defined as a violation with a detection? [Coverage, Spec FR-111 NAC] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK007 - Does the clarification request define its content (options, impact per option)? [Completeness, Scenario C §4] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is the decision record required (who, rationale, inputs, affected artifacts)? [Completeness, Spec FR-108] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-decision-lineage}
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the resume point defined as the stage that consumed the ambiguous content, with carried-over nodes? [Clarity, Spec FR-113, Scenario C §4] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK010 - Must downstream impacts be identified and affected artifacts updated, with stale marking? [Coverage, Spec SCN-C] [M, G0]

## Variants, Outcomes, Evidence

- [ ] CHK011 - Are the unanswered, late, and rejected variants (C-F2..C-F6) defined with expected terminal outcomes (SAFE_STOPPED, CANCELLED) and late-response rejection? [Coverage, Scenario C §6, Spec DEC-041] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the no-change terminal outcome (COMPLETED, NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED) defined with skipped-node reasons? [Completeness, Scenario C §9] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is embedded-instruction input defined with an expected refusal? [Edge Case, Security TH-06] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is the human decision required at run time, not predetermined? [Clarity, Scenario C intro] [M, G0] {Detects: fabricated-results}
- [ ] CHK015 - Do Scenario C evidence artifacts have defined contents under evidence/scenario-c, with simulated timeouts labelled? [Completeness, Scenario C §8, Spec DEC-044, DEC-100] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the change variant labelled documented but not planned? [Coverage, Scenario C §4] [O, G0]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` or `[Conflict]` name a place where the current documents are silent or disagree; they are findings for the reviewer to resolve, not pre-judged results
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially within this file (`CHK001` onward); cite them as `<file>:CHKnnn`
